What

What Emergency Tree Removal Involves

Emergency tree removal is response-time work. The line that separates an emergency from a same-week scheduled removal is whether the tree is currently causing damage, actively blocking emergency-vehicle access, or in imminent danger of doing so. Roubic's 24/7 emergency line dispatches from our Auburn Township yard with crane support, trained climbers, and a full debris-haul fleet.

The scenarios that qualify: a tree on a house, garage, vehicle, or outbuilding; a fallen trunk blocking a driveway or roadway; a leaning tree with visible root-plate movement; or storm-split branches over occupied living space. For trees in contact with active power lines we coordinate with FirstEnergy / The Illuminating Company before any work begins.

Why

Four Reasons NE Ohio Calls the Emergency Line

The scenarios Roubic's 24/7 line handles most across NE Ohio properties.

Tree on a Structure

House, garage, vehicle, or outbuilding. Crane-assisted extraction with tarp-coverage of any roof opening.

Fallen Tree Blocking Access

A trunk across the driveway or road that blocks emergency-vehicle access needs immediate clearance.

Leaning Tree, Root-Plate Movement

Visible root-plate lift after saturated ground or wind means the tree can fail without warning.

Storm-Split Crown Over Living Space

Major branches or a split crown hanging over occupied rooms after storm damage.

Common Emergency Questions

Emergency Tree Removal FAQ

Five things NE Ohio homeowners ask before calling the emergency line.

How do I reach Roubic in an emergency?
Call {{global.phone}} — live answer 24/7. Our emergency line dispatches directly from the Auburn Township yard. Do not enter a damaged area until the crew arrives; branch shifts can be unpredictable.
What's the response time for emergency tree removal?
Target on-site response window inside our Tier 1/2 service area is 2–4 hours, conditions permitting. Tier 3 markets (Chesterland, Mayfield, South Russell) carry a brief mobilization premium for emergency work.
How much does emergency tree removal cost?
Emergency response pricing depends on access, equipment required, and tree-on-structure complexity. Most insurance-coverable jobs land between $1,200 and $8,000. Crane-assisted tree-on-house extraction for heritage canopy can exceed $10,000. Roubic's documentation package is built to meet carrier requirements on the first submission.
Will Roubic dispatch during a high-wind event?
No — crew safety prohibits climber and crane deployment during active high-wind conditions or lightning. Once conditions are safe (typically 2–4 hours after the storm passes), we dispatch aggressively across multiple jobs in priority order.
What if a tree falls on my house?
Call {{global.phone}} immediately. We dispatch with crane support for extraction, photograph the scene for insurance, perform tarp-coverage of any roof opening, and coordinate full extraction and cleanup. Don't enter the damaged area until the crew arrives.
